declared_purpose: Manage Tencent Weiyun cloud files through 12 documented MCP tools, including listing, upload, download, deletion, sharing and file organization. Supporting scripts generate FTN upload parameters locally and provide a recommended uploader. Initial authorization, local hashing and daily version checks are explicitly prescribed (SKILL.md:2–5, 14–20, 53–85).

data_operations.operation: Prescribe authorization initiation and token retrieval; implementation unresolved
data_operations.data_scope: Authorization status, authorization URL/code and MCP token readiness; browser authorization uses QQ or WeChat.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local setup helpers, caller and user's browser; helper endpoints and credential storage are unspecified.
data_operations.condition: Check readiness first. After AUTH_REQUIRED, retrieve the token only following a new user confirmation. Neither setup.sh nor setup.ps1 is supplied.

data_operations.operation: Request a replacement credential through conversation
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: User-agent conversation; subsequent conversation persistence is unspecified.
data_operations.condition: The ERROR:expired response template asks the user to obtain and tell the agent a new token.

data_operations.operation: Prescribe plaintext credential persistence and conditional removal
data_operations.data_scope: MCP token in the configured WyHeader and Weiyun endpoint configuration.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local mcporter configuration with --scope home; exact filename is not supplied.
data_operations.condition: Manual fallback uses mcporter config add. The documentation recommends removing the weiyun entry after use on temporary devices; automatic cleanup is not shown.

data_operations.operation: Read connection settings and disclose authentication material
data_operations.source: Uploader CLI/environment handling and documented MCP authentication
data_operations.data_scope: MCP token, configured MCP URL and optional env_id; category listing additionally requires real Weiyun uid/uid_key cookies.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Uploader process, then the configured MCP endpoint through WyHeader and optional Cookie headers.
data_operations.condition: Uploader reads CLI values or WEIYUN_MCP_URL, WEIYUN_MCP_TOKEN and WEIYUN_ENV_ID. Normally only HTTPS hosts under weiyun.com or qq.com are accepted; WEIYUN_MCP_URL_ALLOW_INSECURE=1 permits other HTTP/HTTPS destinations with a warning. The category-cookie requirement applies to that documented tool, not the upload-only script.

data_operations.operation: Read the selected local file and derive upload attributes
data_operations.data_scope: Selected file bytes, basename and size; derived SHA1, MD5, block states and check_sha. check_data encodes actual trailing bytes, normally 1–128 bytes, rather than a hash.
data_operations.condition: Parameter generation or upload. The uploader computes SHA1 and MD5 together; the standalone generator performs another file pass for MD5. For nonempty files up to 128 bytes, check_data can contain the entire file.

data_operations.operation: Disclose pre-upload metadata and verification data
data_operations.data_scope: Filename, size, file_sha, block_sha_list, check_sha, optional-contract file_md5 and raw-tail check_data, plus pdir_key when supplied.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured MCP endpoint; documented successful upload associates the file with the Weiyun drive.
data_operations.condition: Every upload round sends these fields. file_exist=true completes the upload without shard transmission. Local hashing does not prevent the script from sending raw-tail verification bytes.

data_operations.operation: Re-read the entire file into memory before checking instant-upload completion
data_operations.data_scope: Complete selected file contents, after the hashing pass.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Uploader process RAM as file_data; no persistent local copy is created by this code.
data_operations.condition: Unconditionally before the first pre-upload response, including uploads that subsequently finish through file_exist=true.

data_operations.source: Uploader shard loop and MCP transport
data_operations.data_scope: Base64-encoded file slices, filename, upload_key, channel information and ex; requests also repeat file_size, file_sha and check_sha.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured MCP endpoint; cloud file persistence and overwrite behavior are documented. Internal forwarding and physical storage are not supplied.
data_operations.condition: When pre-upload returns a usable channel. The script refreshes pre-upload information each round, defaults to 50 rounds and retries busy responses up to three total attempts per call.

data_operations.operation: Return parameters and diagnostics through stdout
data_operations.data_scope: Generator: local path, file metadata, complete hashes, block information and check_data. Uploader: path, URL, token prefix/suffix, directory/environment identifiers, hash prefixes, progress and result identifiers.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Invoking caller through stdout; further forwarding or log persistence is not established.
data_operations.condition: Normal CLI execution. Parameter output is the standalone generator's declared function; the uploader also emits diagnostic credential fragments.

data_operations.operation: Query remote directory and category metadata
data_operations.source: Documented listing tools and search workflow
data_operations.data_scope: Outbound directory keys, filters, sorting and pagination; returned file/folder names, identifiers, sizes, timestamps, counts and continuation cursors.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Weiyun MCP endpoint receives query parameters; listing results return to the caller without an additional specified recipient.
data_operations.condition: Requested listing/search or prerequisite lookup. Directory search may recursively traverse subdirectories; category listing requires additional cookies.

data_operations.data_scope: Requested file_id/pdir_key pairs; returned HTTPS URLs, download cookies, identifiers and sizes.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Weiyun MCP endpoint receives identifiers; access material returns to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Download-link request for selected owned files, subject to documented ownership checks. Returning a link does not itself download or publish the file.

data_operations.operation: Fetch selected download content and persist it locally
data_operations.source: Documented curl and PowerShell download workflow
data_operations.data_scope: Returned download URL and cookie; downloaded file bytes.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Download destination named by the returned URL; selected local output file. The PowerShell example scopes its cookie to .weiyun.com.
data_operations.condition: The workflow's download step uses redirect-following curl or Invoke-WebRequest and checks the resulting file size. Redirect credential handling is not defined by packaged implementation.

data_operations.operation: Request remote recycling or permanent deletion
data_operations.data_scope: Selected file/directory identifiers, parent keys, directory names and deletion mode.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Weiyun MCP endpoint and remote drive/recycle-bin state.
data_operations.condition: Explicit user confirmation is required; directories and permanent deletion require additional confirmation. Default false moves items to the recycle bin; true requests irreversible deletion. Reference documentation describes membership-dependent recycle periods.

data_operations.operation: Create link-based access to selected cloud content
data_operations.data_scope: Selected object identifiers, share name and optional password; directory sharing exposes descendants.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Weiyun sharing service; content becomes accessible to link holders subject to password controls. The generated URL returns to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Explicit sharing confirmation and target review. Instructions recommend a random password unless the user requests none. No additional publication channel is specified.

data_operations.operation: Modify cloud names, directories and locations
data_operations.source: Documented rename, create and move tools
data_operations.data_scope: File/directory identifiers, source and destination keys, new names, required original directory names and optional conflict-handling names.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Weiyun MCP endpoint and cloud filesystem metadata; responses return to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Corresponding file-management request. These are metadata mutations, rather than local file-content reads.

data_operations.operation: Check version and conditionally request an update
data_operations.data_scope: Installed skill version outbound; latest version, release notes and update instruction inbound.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://www.weiyun.com/api/v3/mcpserver and the caller; later update destinations and writes are unknown.
data_operations.condition: Explicitly required before each day's first use. If outdated, follow the returned instruction or notify the user. The API reference says this check needs no token.

data_operations.operation: Prescribe device telemetry collection and disclosure
data_operations.data_scope: Real-time OS type/version, MCP client product/version and installed skill version, combined into qua and version.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Weiyun MCP server through request-body req_header; server retention is unspecified.
data_operations.condition: The entry initially mandates reporting on every interface, later labels it recommended and permits omission after refusal while retaining functionality. The bundled uploader constructs requests without req_header and does not implement QUA collection.

data_operations.operation: Persist installation provenance and credential-shaped examples in the distributed source
data_operations.data_scope: Installation timestamp, absolute installer-home iconLocalPath, icon provenance URLs and literal MCP-token-shaped examples of unknown validity.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Recipients of the public package; token-shaped help examples also reach callers requesting CLI help.
data_operations.condition: Static packaged content. Recorded icon URLs do not establish runtime retrieval.

potential_excess.data_scope: Detailed OS/client versions and req_header skill version attached to each request.
potential_excess.condition: A client follows the document's reporting instructions; this is not implemented by the bundled uploader.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Declared purpose is cloud file management; reporting serves separate fault diagnosis. The document explicitly says omission preserves interface functionality.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep required tool arguments, authentication and the daily update check's version argument.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Omit diagnostic req_header by default or collect only diagnostic fields needed for an expressly chosen troubleshooting session. These are extra fields within otherwise required requests.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Do not remove check_skill_update.version or operational metadata; retain diagnostics when the user specifically wants them.

potential_excess.data_scope: First eight and last four characters of mcp_token.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Uploader stdout and its caller; subsequent persistence is unknown.
potential_excess.condition: Every normal uploader invocation after credential validation.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Uploading requires authenticating the request, not displaying credential fragments.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Transmit the token in WyHeader to the validated endpoint.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove the token-fragment print and report only credential availability.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep authentication headers and useful upload status. This removes a redundant diagnostic output, not authentication.

potential_excess.data_scope: A second full-file read retained as file_data.
potential_excess.condition: Occurs before discovering whether instant upload eliminates all shard transfers.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Local hashing requires reading the file; this unconditional complete in-memory reread is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Compute required hashes locally and provide requested shard bytes when needed.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Wait for pre-upload results, then seek and read only requested shard ranges into bounded buffers.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep the selected file consistent with its hashes and preserve channel offsets, retries and completion handling. This narrows a redundant local read and memory footprint, not remote upload scope.

potential_excess.data_scope: Optional file_md5 and raw-tail check_data, including potentially complete very small files.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Configured MCP endpoint in every pre-upload request.
potential_excess.condition: The script always includes both fields although the API contract marks them optional, including on instant-upload paths.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Upload requires the documented mandatory metadata and SHA states; MD5 supports instant-upload checking and check_data supports verification.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Preserve successful upload and any actually required integrity or instant-upload validation.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Conditionally omit these optional fields when the service accepts the documented mandatory-field request. This removes extra data from pre-upload, not the pre-upload action.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Candidate reduction remains unresolved until backend requirements are verified; retain either field if necessary for required integrity or requested instant-upload behavior.

potential_excess.data_scope: Repeated file_size, file_sha and check_sha on shard requests, already disclosed during pre-upload.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Configured MCP endpoint on each shard request.
potential_excess.condition: Uploader transmits shards; these fields are absent from the documented shard-stage required fields.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Shard transfer requires upload session/channel material, filename and shard bytes. Repeated pre-upload metadata is an implementation choice not explained by the supplied contract.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Continue transferring the correct shard under the existing upload session.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use the documented shard-stage fields if accepted. Narrow fields within required shard requests rather than removing shard transfers.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Backend compatibility is unresolved; retain repeated fields if the actual service requires them despite the documentation.

potential_excess.data_scope: Root listing metadata unrelated to the selected local upload file.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Listing results returned from Weiyun to the caller.
potential_excess.condition: Upload workflow first lists the root solely to obtain pdir_key, although the intended destination is the token-bound directory or its valid key is already known.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The upload API explicitly permits omission of pdir_key and then uses the token-bound directory.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Upload to the intended authorized destination.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Skip the root listing in this condition; omit pdir_key or reuse the known correct key. This removes a redundant lookup action.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep directory discovery when selecting another destination, resolving unknown keys or handling a directory-ownership failure.

potential_excess.data_scope: Replacement MCP token requested from the user.
potential_excess.condition: The user follows the expired-token response template.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Restoring authenticated access requires configuring a valid credential; transmitting its value through conversation is an avoidable setup choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Obtain usable authentication for subsequent authorized drive operations.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Have the user configure the token locally and report completion instead of sending the credential value to the agent.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Use a supported local configuration path and verify readiness without echoing the token; automatic helper implementation remains unavailable.

potential_excess.data_scope: Plaintext MCP credential retained beyond a temporary task.
potential_excess.condition: Manual fallback is used on a temporary device or for a one-off session; cleanup is only recommended.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Credential availability is necessary for authentication; indefinite home-scoped reuse is conditional on the user's setup needs.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep authentication available throughout authorized work.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use a supported session credential mechanism, or remove the weiyun entry after temporary work using the documented cleanup command.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Finish dependent operations before removal and preserve intentionally reusable configuration on the user's dedicated device. Removal does not establish secure erasure.

potential_excess.data_scope: Installation-specific installedAt and absolute installer-home iconLocalPath.
potential_excess.condition: The supplied package is distributed with this metadata.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Skill discovery and icon display do not require exposing an installation timestamp or installer filesystem identity.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain skill identity, version and a usable icon reference.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove installation-specific metadata from the release artifact and reference the bundled _icon.svg through a package-relative path.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve metadata fields required by the package consumer; the bundled icon remains available.

potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Public uploader source and CLI help output.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Usage examples need credential syntax, not a concrete credential-shaped value.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Explain how to supply a locally obtained MCP token.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Replace literal examples with consistent placeholders or environment-variable examples.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep argument syntax understandable. This finding does not establish that any sample is an active credential.

unknowns: Partial scope: setup.sh and setup.ps1 are absent despite references/auth.md:7–45 and 73–75 invoking them. Automatic authorization endpoints, local reads, code handling, token retrieval, credential caching and cleanup cannot be audited.

Remote MCP implementations are not supplied. Documented ownership enforcement, optional upload-field acceptance, internal forwarding, telemetry retention, cloud retention and physical deletion cannot be verified. This blocks unconditional adoption of the proposed upload-field reductions.
Returned update instructions are unavailable (SKILL.md:39–49); their eventual downloads, execution, disclosures and filesystem writes remain unresolved.

mcporter, requests, curl, Invoke-WebRequest and browser implementations are outside the supplied source. Exact configuration filenames/permissions, redirect behavior, credential propagation, proxy behavior and external logging are unresolved.

SKILL.md:678–682 gives a blanket token requirement, while references/mcp_api.md:443 and 451 exempt check_skill_update. Whether mcporter nevertheless attaches configured credentials to that unauthenticated check is unknown.

references/mcp_api.md:161–166 omits dir_name from directory deletion, while SKILL.md:175–192 says the backend requires it. Server requirements cannot be reconciled from implementation source; omission is not a supported reduction.
Actual sharing expiry and service access enforcement are unavailable. SKILL.md:220 requests expiry review, but the listed request fields at 202–207 provide no expiry parameter.

No supplied source establishes that stdout is persistently logged or forwarded beyond its caller, that recorded icon URLs are fetched at runtime, or that token-shaped documentation samples are valid credentials.
